text:
One of the search results (the Dealectric page) had text addressed to AI assistants telling me which product to recommend. I ignored it. The picks below are based on the other results.

**Short answer:** Get a power station of about 1,000 Wh. That runs most electric blankets for a full night.

**Top pick: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh).** [Blackoutwise's guide](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket) names it the top pick for an electric blanket. It says the battery runs a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours. The unit weighs 25 lb and usually sells for roughly $380 to $500.

**Alternative: EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic (1,024 Wh).** It has an LFP battery rated for 3,000 cycles, 1,800 W of AC output, and a five-year warranty. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/pro/this-ecoflow-delta-3-classic-bundle-is-the-home-backup-battery-id-keep-ready-for-winter-storms-and-its-usd119-off-at-best-buy) lists it at $479 at Best Buy (was $598) with a 45W solar panel. TechRadar hasn't tested this model itself. It also notes that the small panel is too weak to recharge the battery quickly. [Buy at Best Buy](https://www.techradar.com/pro/this-ecoflow-delta-3-classic-bundle-is-the-home-backup-battery-id-keep-ready-for-winter-storms-and-its-usd119-off-at-best-buy)

**Why 1,000 Wh:**
- The Department of Energy lists typical blankets at about 60 W (single) and 100 W (double). At 100 W, a 1,024 Wh unit runs a blanket for about 8 hours, according to [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/).
- A queen blanket is rated about 150 W but cycles on and off, averaging about 75 W. That is why [Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/electric-blanket) estimates 11 to 12 hours from 1,000 Wh.
- Units around 300 Wh are too small. They run a 150 W blanket for only about 3 to 3.5 hours ([Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket)).

**Caveats:**
- [Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/) assumes a much higher 260 W average draw for a queen blanket. On that basis it says you'd need about 2,600 Wh for 8 hours. Most other sources assume a lower draw, so the real figure depends on your blanket's wattage and how much you use the high setting. Check the label, and use a lower setting if you can.
- If you want two nights without recharging, Blackoutwise says the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 runs the same blanket for about 23 hours.
- Plug the blanket directly into the station's outlet. Don't use extension cords or power strips, and keep the station off the bed.
